note: Benefit rates change in the first full week of April, NOT 1 April. See spec §11 for the boundary problem.

guardiansAllowance.eligibilityNote: Both parents dead, or one dead and the other untraceable / serving 2+ years / whereabouts unknown. Parental UK residence condition applies.

universalCredit.childElementNote: Two rates, not one. A first child born before 6 April 2017 keeps the higher protected rate; every other child gets the standard element.
universalCredit.statute: Universal Credit (Removal of Two Child Limit) Act 2026 c.13

qualifyingCareRelief.note: QCR is for foster and shared-lives carers. A former foster carer still fostering OTHER children uses QCR for that income only.

sgoAllowanceTaxTreatment.note: Treated as a residence-order allowance; exempt from income tax since 6 April 2010.

incomeSupportApplicableAmounts.note: Weekly rates exactly as printed in DWP 'Benefit and pension rates 2026 to 2027' (updated 16 February 2026). Income Support is a legacy benefit largely closed to new claims, yet the DfE model anchors core living costs to it. That is a fair criticism of the model rather than a reason not to implement it, and it is why MEANS_TEST_MODEL_OUTDATED fires on every result that uses this.

sourcedButUnused.note: Published in the same table and recorded so nobody has to re-source them. Not read by the engine: each would need its own question in the finances step before it could be applied honestly.

capitalRules.note: Confirms the capital model the spec carried as an unsourced assumption. DEFAULT_CAPITAL in meansTest.ts must agree with these; a unit test asserts it.
capitalRules.tariffAsPrinted: £1 for every £250, or part thereof, between the amount of capital disregarded and the capital upper limit.
